trust_decision.summary: Whether the current user may perform GET on this view must be decided before AdminRenderer fabricates a GET to populate a 400 error page; the fix decides it with view.check_permissions(request) run on the GET-cloned request inside AdminRenderer.render (object-level access is then re-checked inside get_object).

landing_point.why: the summary names AdminRenderer rendering invalid write requests; the only code that produces that page is the status==400 branch, whose one unusual act is simulating a GET and taking response.data from it

fix_sites.entry_point: HTML rendering of any DRF view that lists AdminRenderer in renderer_classes and answers POST/PUT/PATCH with 400 (admin.html error page)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The other data-bearing surface on the same 400 page (the bound edit/raw form, renderers.py:786-789 -> 477-496) is gated on the write method, and a user who may PUT/PATCH an object is arguably entitled to see the fields they are allowed to write, so it is 'not a read path'.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: For a user who *is* permitted to GET, the 400 page must still show the list/detail representation next to the validation error; the fix keeps the simulated GET unless check_permissions raises, and its first regression test asserts the GET content is still rendered (fix.diff:49-78). A fix that drops the simulated GET outright, or skips it whenever permission_classes is non-default, breaks this.

O6_input_shapes: error detail that is a dict (field-keyed validation errors) - used as-is for the page
error detail that is not a dict (e.g. a list of ErrorDetail) - wrapped under api_settings.NON_FIELD_ERRORS_KEY (fix.diff:24-25)
validation error raised by serializer.is_valid(raise_exception=True) versus a view raising serializers.ValidationError directly (both exercised by the fix's second and third tests, fix.diff:80-144)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: The 400 page's edit/raw form is derived from data.serializer.instance (renderers.py:477-483, 488-493, 525-527) and rendered through serializer.data (renderers.py:544-556, 599), so it shows the object's own field values; its gate is show_form_for_method(view, <write method>, ...) (renderers.py:446-459) which checks permission for PUT/PATCH, never for GET. A user allowed to write but denied GET therefore still sees the object representation on an invalid write when the view returns 400 carrying a serializer bound to that instance.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: A user who can PUT/PATCH the object can already see those fields through that form, so the edit form is not a disclosure route - and the advisory text only mentions the simulated GET.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same file, about 300 lines above the fix site (renderers.py:446-556 vs 786-794); reached through the inherited BrowsableAPIRenderer.get_context, so the browsable API shares it

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A version of get_rendered_html_form that, when a 400 carries no serializer, fetches current state with view.get(view.request, *view.args, **view.kwargs) to prefill the edit form
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The method already exists to build a form from view.get_serializer(instance=...) and the AdminRenderer 400 branch already simulates a GET for exactly the same purpose (show current state), so a maintainer adding prefilled error forms would copy renderers.py:792-794

O8b_injection_room.sibling: get_raw_data_form prefilling the PUT/PATCH textarea with the object representation obtained via a simulated GET when the write failed
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: This method already renders serializer.data for the instance (renderers.py:599) and already wraps itself in override_method, so the extra simulated fetch is a one-line addition in existing style

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second admin-style renderer (e.g. a delete-confirmation or print/export renderer subclassing BrowsableAPIRenderer) that renders the resource on a failed write without the permission gate
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: AdminRenderer is a thin subclass of BrowsableAPIRenderer; adding a sibling renderer that shows 'the record you tried to delete/export' is the obvious extension of this feature and would repeat the simulate-GET idiom

O9_family: CWE-200 information disclosure (authorization bypass in a presentation/render layer: GET-protected representation data exposed on an invalid write response)

O10_build.toolchain: pip install -e . plus pytest (runtests.py / tox); Django 4.x-5.x with pytest-django; the patch's new names (exceptions, api_settings) are already imported at rest_framework/renderers.py:23,29
O10_build.project_tests: tests/test_renderers.py::AdminRendererTests (7 tests at the pinned commit, driven by APIRequestFactory + response.render()); none of them covers a 400 write response or permissions, and the three tests the fix adds are absent from the pinned tree

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Remove or blanket-disable the simulated GET in the 400 branch (or gate it on 'permission_classes is non-default'), which hides the resource representation from users who are allowed to read it and breaks the must-keep-working behaviour that the error page still shows list/detail data.

out_of_scope_notes: rest_framework/schemas/generators.py:236 and rest_framework/metadata.py:82 gate schema/metadata output on view.check_permissions - an adjacent information-disclosure surface, outside this advisory's renderer scope; noted only, not pursued.
